I'm a total beginner at fighting games, but judging from the public perception, it's a great fighting game overall, aside some balancing issues.

Personally, I can say it's got 2 great things I've been trying to find in a fighting game:

1. It's easy to pick up, but not shallow. This is thanks to the general design direction of the game: each character has a unique, but compact movelist; there is a good mode for learning all of the different mechanics; the damage is adjusted to be high, which makes the game seem easier; the floor system actually works, despite some problems with connection etc.
2. And it's simply fun! I don't really know how to describe it much, but I've had a lot of fun with it, even if I didn't really take it too seriously.

And last but not least, the game has a good and active community with lots of quality resources for begginers.

Strive is a great fighting game that has a relatively low skill floor but a decently high skill ceiling. Pretty much all of the characters feel pretty good to control and the visuals are great, while the game is also pretty friendly to those that don't necessarily have a whole lot of experience with fighting games. Strive is pretty much the first fighting game that i really picked up seriously enough to really try and improve at, and so far it's been a great journey.

I'm not saying the game is perfectly balanced, nor am i saying that there aren't characters that are just not that fun to fight against, but being able to pick up a character and almost instantly feel comfortable with their moves and mechanics is not something many fighting games have been able to provide for me. Strive managed to do this, and along with the crazy lore and amazing soundtrack and visuals, i just have nothing but praise for this game (even if i occasionally bitch about some of the less fun mechanics haha)

Coming from melee, Strive is my first '2D fighter' I took serious.
I personally like to grind out some combo's in training mode and get a kick out of landing them in a real match.

Another feature that attracted me is the rollback netcode implemented within the game.
Basically it's a type of network configuration (in my opinion) optimal for fighting games.

I can't speak for 1P mode and/or a more casual approach.

There are characters who can seem cheesy and/or feel unbeatable at times, but with the replay feature and training mode you should be able to 'lab' out these situations and improve on them.

The ranked system is not perfect BUT, it prevents higher ranked players stomping the lower ranked area's.

Things to consider:
- The startup of the game is some slow, due to network configurations on their server side. (Good ol' windows XP experience).
- I've head that some people have some connectivity issues during matches, personally I haven't

So far, I have made one person on my friends list uninstall the game at least once and another endlessly proclaim that strive sucks and that x or y is better about three times now.

Personally, I'm having a great time and enjoy playing a character that I've never seen anyone play online and no one really seems to remember what he does (Zato)
